# Prepublication interruption boundary for examination

Source 026ba3db, code 70688b60. Round 4 closed CR6–CR8 and found one at-capacity proof gap, CR9. This note raises a source-derived question, not a measured defect verdict or authority to expand the frozen mandate.

The frozen O2/D5 contract covers surviving children after an unconfirmed shutdown and resources resolved before provenance publication. Current catalog_uses is an in-memory map, reset by PathAuthority::open. Only CatalogInstall.users is persisted. Before any install exists, resolving an explicit recursive directory resource cannot add a session marker to an install record. EngineRuntime's kill_on_drop cannot help on process death, as process.rs:3771 explains, and Linux pre_exec only preserves descriptors, not a parent-death kill guarantee.

Candidate counterexample: session A hands the engine workspace directory to a real child as an explicit recursive resource while no catalog install is present. A stops unconfirmed before any install provenance exists. Child A can survive, still holding the directory. Session B opens the same registry, whose process-use map is empty, and trusted reconciliation may prune the now-unowned resource authority. B publishes a later catalog install under that directory, then cancels its save. B exits cleanly and clears only its own markers. Session C trusts its owner snapshot and collects the unowned new install. Does this delete underneath the earlier child despite O2, or does a specific frozen threat-model exclusion or actual lifecycle producer prevent this scenario?

Read actual plan wording and actual producers before judging. Do not assume every engine exits on stdin EOF, because D5 explicitly refuses restart as proof that children exited. No source claim that old processes can be safely guessed absent. Directory resources are explicit recursive ownership, distinct from arbitrary filesystem permissions or an incidental executable working directory. This is the same profile, no deliberate cross-profile/manual sharing of a managed install tree.

If this is within the frozen obligation, examine the simplest faithful correction: unresolved prepublication recursive-resource use must have durable bounded evidence before handoff even when there is no install record yet. Keep it in the existing registry, never a second journal or per-actor lease system, retain actual terminal binding and session, clear only the originating session after proven shutdown, and have future publication account for prior unresolved uses. Consider whether existing native authority state can hold that evidence without a second implementation of use ownership, and whether per-install markers can share a single mechanism. Do not write code or silently impose a new scope. Explain the minimum contract change and concrete proof needed, or identify the exact source/decision that makes the counterexample impossible or out of mandate.

CR9 remains an independent accepted test gap, do not lose it. Required future proof for this question, if in scope, would retain a real inherited directory lease across registry reopen BEFORE publication, then publish and perform a later trusted reopen after the newer session clears its own markers, with the original child still alive and reaped safely. No actual process abort is needed to model the durable-state boundary. Plan authorship and arbitration shared one context. Detection uses the same model family as code.

Use the shared relation for retained authority bindings and session uses. When known historical identity exists, it participates in physical membership and disjointness. Match a recursive resource identity against actual target ancestor identities, including the target's verified parent before publication. If its current pathname is missing or resolves to another identity, that replacement cannot establish disjointness of the original use. Preserve uncertainty unless positive actual binding evidence establishes membership or disjointness. Do not convert such uncertainty into cleaning refusal. Preserve CR6's identity-distinct replacements, exact absent cleaning reservation, unrelated engine isolation, marker persistence refusal and all deletion boundaries. No unchecked pathname becomes deletion authority.

# CR6 mechanism correction

Cleaning adoption refusal requires positive membership evidence instead of a failed lookup of some other tree. The private helper arrangement remains an implementation detail. The behavioral boundary is that one unavailable cleaning root cannot prevent unrelated engine resolution, yet actual cleaning-tree adoption remains refused under lexical and filesystem-alias relationships, including a moved tree where its identity can be proven. Uncertain trees remain retained and successful child handoff still requires durable conservative use evidence.

Required proof adds an actual missing or renamed cleaning root alongside an independently installed executable, verifies successful unrelated resolution and preserved cleaning provenance, and verifies actual moved or aliased cleaning descendants remain refused. Existing retained, session, prepublication alias, retry, admission, modified partial-tree and shutdown tests remain green. New regressions must fail behaviorally with only their source fix removed. Windows/macOS runtime remains hosted proof.

This is a focused mechanism judgment required by push-review-policy 4a before another patch. It is not a new product requirement, a new build lineage or a repetition of settled plan review. #### mechanism-cwd-handoff.md

````text
# CR12 native cwd handoff correction

Private implementation mechanism candidate cwd1 at committed snapshot a88febeb1028854420bbf974f8bbdb4f4056f6e6. Frozen O1–O4 and d-20261016-11 remain unchanged. This is a focused implementation check after cumulative round5, not a new inherited-plan round. No source changes since that review.

Defect and evidence

Correctness and engine-protocol independently identify one gap. mod.rs:7870 records resolved.parent_identity in durable node evidence. engine_executable:6743 then retains a pathname as working_directory, and process.rs:3766 calls current_dir on it during later spawn. A completed parent replacement after resolution can start the pinned Linux image in a different managed tree. Its identity is absent from the recorded image/cwd node set, so the tree can be eligible after interruption even while the child uses relative data. The ordinary-operation threat includes a single completed substitution, without continuous malicious mutation. Source-derived scenario, no runtime reproduction yet. Existing cwd regression starts before moving its directory, so it misses this handoff.

Required shared contract

The working directory used for launch must be the same validated directory object whose identity was durably recorded before handoff. It stays owned by the EngineExecutable through the existing child cleanup owner until confirmed reaping. A stale pathname must never substitute another cwd. Do not broaden cwd to recursive ambient ownership or reintroduce blanket stale-node retention. Keep canonical authorization, image/resource sealing, spawn admission, physical ownership, all failure cleanup and deadlines.

Candidate

Carry the already validated retained parent descriptor from ResolvedPath into EngineExecutable rather than dropping it. Reuse parent() and a fallible clone or a private transfer accessor, never reopen a pathname to establish identity. The same object supplied parent_identity at the durable use boundary.

On Unix, set cwd by fchdir of this retained descriptor in the fork child immediately before exec, using the existing command pre_exec boundary. fchdir and the existing Linux fcntl loop are async-signal-safe. Do not change the parent's process cwd or use a global cwd lock. Unix spawn must not first depend on pathname current_dir, because a moved original directory should remain usable by descriptor. Linux continues inheriting only its existing image/resources descriptors, not a new ambient capability. macOS keeps existing managed image/file-resource materialization and uses the same Unix cwd object binding.

On Windows, retain the validated parent handle that was opened by open_windows_nofollow without FILE_SHARE_DELETE, alongside the existing sealed executable handle and launch pathname. Keep it through CreateProcess and the same owner lifetime. The held no-delete parent prevents its completed replacement while path-based CreateProcess establishes cwd. Verify this against actual Windows runtime tests, including parent and containing-directory rename attempts. If the existing handle sharing cannot seal the pathname binding, the candidate needs a narrowly stronger existing native open boundary before acceptance, not a check-then-spawn pathname race or an invented runtime claim. Do not add a registry or process-global lock.

Private field/accessor shape is executor-owned. Test fixtures must supply a real held cwd boundary without breaking deliberate spawn-failure cases. Existing canonical path authorization is still performed. Do not bypass workspace_entry_path or widen operation/capability scope.

Proof obligations

Add a real Linux child regression that resolves an executable and records its cwd, performs the reported completed replacement before spawn, then starts the actual app-owned Actor. Original cwd data is readable through relative access, replacement data is never consumed. Where useful restore exact managed-tree locator, root/parent/tree/inventory identities before trusted reopen to prove replacement tree remains collectible without affecting original child data. No separate directory-resource lease may mask cwd evidence. Source-only remove only the launch binding correction with all new tests unchanged, compiled behavioral red, exact restore green. Parent reaps the child before propagating every captured failure. Preserve existing removed-image cwd, historical recursive resource and three-session witnesses.

Unix/macOS tests prove original object or explicit safe refusal after movement, never substitute a different cwd. Windows tests attempt parent and ancestor replacement while EngineExecutable is held, assert no successful substituted launch and retain a normal native cwd positive control. Hosted rust-windows-test and rust-macos-test provide actual runtime proof, local Windows GNU compilation alone is insufficient. No claim of runtime approval before those jobs.

Also address independent round5 corrections in the same source package after mechanism approval: CR13 rename only the aggregate snapshot/counter to admission-unit names while keeping the genuinely unique_registry_id_count helper named correctly, preserve arithmetic/bounds. CR14 seed the capacity fixture using actual canonical authority-issued bindings, retain production overflow and usable reuse plus both guard reversals. CR15 derive expected image/cwd keys from validated registered binding rather than raw Windows temp spelling. Root handles CR16 records qualification.

Reversal path

If descriptor cwd is unavailable, return a typed pre-spawn error with cleanup, never silently fall back to a substituted pathname. If future evidence requires path-based semantics, it must include an equivalent object-binding proof and child lifetime preservation.

Concrete Linux interleaving: publish an unowned managed tree T, resolve an independent engine in directory A, then move A aside and temporarily move T onto A’s pathname before spawn. The engine executes A’s pinned image but starts inside T. Restore both directories after spawn, then interrupt the application while that child survives. On restart, durable image/cwd evidence identifies A, so T is classified Disjoint and its unchanged inventory permits deletion while the child still uses T for relative data. The cwd regression starts the child before moving its directory and does not cover this handoff mismatch. Native regressions

Seven new context1 tests remain, bringing the catalog selector from 65 to 72 tests.

- `catalog_install_context1_eligibility_rechecks_completed_ancestor_substitution` uses the app-owned real inherited-directory child. Its image and cwd are in a separate probe directory. A's explicit resource is unrelated at publication, with no A-derived marker and every A use classified Disjoint then. B retires the resource through production attachment reconciliation and completes the real successful shutdown wrapper. A completed substitution moves an unchanged intermediate container under the leased directory and restores the original absolute root path. The test proves unchanged root identity, immediate-parent identity, tree identity and complete inventory. C opens afterward, trusts startup owners and retains data the child reads through its real inherited descriptor.
- `catalog_install_context1_stale_file_nodes_do_not_own_unrelated_installs` covers both deleted and independently replaced file spellings. A's real explicit File lease stays open across reopen and authority retirement. B publishes an independent tree and clears successfully. C collects that tree, no A marker was projected, A's durable scope survives and the original lease still reads original bytes.
- `catalog_install_context1_removed_image_cwd_keeps_relative_data_without_resource` starts a real image from staging with native cwd and no directory-resource lease. The image is removed before inventory. That same cwd object becomes the managed tree. Reopen and attachment retirement leave relative data readable. The image identity is absent from inventory, while cwd is recorded separately as a node. Removing only cwd capture makes the child lose its relative data.
- `catalog_install_context1_added_file_membership_still_refuses_cleaning` confirms physical membership and typed Conflict for a user-added file absent from managed inventory.
- `catalog_install_context1_image_and_cwd_are_one_durable_handoff` proves one atomic write for both contexts, persisted native identities, zero-install evidence, and write/sync failure refusal with same-binding retries.
- `catalog_install_context1_directory_read_uses_actual_terminal_scope` resolves a directory component through a transient grant without EngineResource root purpose. The selected terminal directory owns nested contents recursively while an unselected sibling remains independent.
- `catalog_install_context1_node_exclusion_still_preserves_changed_inventory` adds a hard link into a published tree, then removes the old node spelling. The node relation is Disjoint, but the independent inventory check preserves both the added bytes and original managed bytes, relinquishing provenance without deleting the changed tree.

The existing inherited-directory probe is shared across old and new tests. Its single UCI loop supports either an explicit resource or actual cwd. The real Actor and Supervisor perform native startup and reaping. Worker failures are captured, and the parent confirms physical reaping before propagating them. A shared Linux-only successful-session helper uses the actual production teardown and catalog-clear wrapper.

  "joiner-plan-r1.md": "# Plan: Retained capability boundaries for puzzle reads and catalog installation\n\n## Goal\nFinish the confirmed co-located capability findings before completing the current drain delivery.\n\n## MANDATE\n### A resolved puzzle capability is unusable after its parent directory is renamed, although it retains the parent handle\n\n* **ID:** f-20260917-05 · **Status:** open · **Area:** native-fs · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none\n* **Where:** `ResolvedPath::puzzle_database_target` (`src-tauri/src/infra/path_authority/resolved.rs:475-500`), whose last step is `canonical_binding(self.target()…)` (`infra/path_authority/mod.rs:1602`); the caller is `puzzle_binding` (`src-tauri/src/puzzle.rs:109`), reached from `cache_key`, the `get_puzzle` loading closure, and `delete_puzzle_database_resolved` (`puzzle.rs:661`).\n* **Defect:** the resolved capability already holds the retained parent descriptor and the leaf name, which is what every later operation actually uses. Minting the carrier nevertheless ends with `canonical_binding`, which calls `fs::canonicalize` on the **parent pathname**. If that parent is renamed after capability resolution, the canonicalization fails with `NotFound` and `puzzle_binding` aborts — before `delete_puzzle_database` gets the chance to use the retained handle, which is still perfectly valid and still names the authorized object. The pathname is needed only for the SQLite URI, the cache key and logging; the deletion path needs none of them.\n* **Why it matters:** the retained descriptor exists precisely so that a pathname change cannot invalidate an authorization. Here a pathname change invalidates it anyway, and the operation that suffers most is deletion, where the user has already confirmed an intent and gets an error naming a path they may have renamed themselves minutes earlier.\n* **Related:** `f-20260914-09` (the Windows port of this function; the defect is identical on unix and is neither introduced nor worsened there, which is why that slice filed it rather than fixing it); `d-20260912-04` recorded that `canonical_binding` canonicalizes only the parent, and this is the consequence of that parent still being resolved by name at mint time.\n* **Found by:** `review-correctness` (99) in round 2 of the `f-20260914-09` plan review, 2026-09-17, on Codex; source-verified by the orchestrator at the lines above, including that the unix arm has the same shape.\n* **Entry revalidation, 2026-10-16:** lens → build. The current read path still loses a resolved parent on rename through puzzle_database_target then DatabaseFileTarget::probe_current. Deletion already has a retained-parent fallback, so its historical failure description is narrowed rather than repeated. The proper correction changes the internal carrier's validation contract for resolved puzzle capabilities while ordinary database carriers retain strict pathname validation and pooled POSIX-lock safety. That is an unsettled shared contract, requiring a reviewed plan within the active full-auto build. It is a confirmed direct-file joiner of reopened f-20260914-12 because both fixes edit resolved.rs, under findings-ledger-contract Ranking6. The original f-20261002-04 frozen plan and metrics remain unchanged.\n* **Open question:** how does DatabaseFileTarget explicitly distinguish a resolved puzzle's retained-parent validation from an ordinary database's strict pathname validation without pathname fallback, leaf reopening or weakening ordinary database containment?\n<!-- ledger-meta {\"command\":\"set-header\",\"effect_lines\":2,\"effect_sha256\":\"bf0a7a0e3b0aba8ff5e7e34a98ed0d0d746847ea1eb801d5d29eb326a263b9b0\",\"header_sha256\":\"5f0ab80aeb88311ffd757d1d94b381d4253039c789d2828dba49581191a5c077\",\"header_status\":\"open\",\"input_sha256\":\"ac8a71de6661392093e7ff1519e76131d024f7b70d8ca0ad89fe82ebf1f3d82c\",\"kind\":\"mutation-receipt\",\"operation\":\"e0ecd67d02f330ce7920b3a022d8375314100b33ba34e093dcb6891dcf495b7c\",\"options\":{\"headers\":{\"Entry\":\"build\"},\"section\":null},\"request_id_sha256\":null,\"results\":[\"f-20260917-05\"],\"target\":\"f-20260917-05\",\"v\":1} -->\n\n### `atomic_install_download_dir` reopens its staging and target directories by path, so the engine-archive install has the same identity-only containment gap as its siblings\n\n* **ID:** f-20260920-01 · **Status:** open · **Area:** native-fs · **Root:** - · **Entry:** lens · **Blocked:** none\n* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/infra/path_authority/resolved.rs` `atomic_install_download_dir` (~:149) and the `private_tempdir_in` / install sequence it drives; consumer `publish_engine_archive_tree` (`src-tauri/src/fs.rs`).\n* **Defect (reported by a lens, confirm before fixing):** the resolved directory identity is dropped and both the temporary directory and the target are reopened by pathname. If the validated engine parent is replaced by another real directory between validation and installation, both reopen under the substitute, the same-parent check still passes, and a signed archive is installed outside the authorised root. Same containment class as `f-20260918-02` (`reserve_download_artifact`, `activate_download_artifact`, `workspace_entry_path`), which does not name this door.\n* **Why it matters:** an engine binary installed outside the workspace the user authorised, from a path the authority believed it had validated.\n* **Fix shape:** the same repair `f-20260917-13` applied to its two doors — `acquire_target` plus an `acquired.path == stored.path` check — carried into the directory-install path; a test that swaps the parent between validation and install must fail the install.\n* **Related:** `f-20260918-02` (same class, sibling doors; Root `-`, so the relation is named here).\n* **Found by:** review-tauri-security (Codex) over the `f-20260906-07` cumulative diff, 2026-09-20; outside that mandate, filed by Claude Code.\n* **Why rejected:** Reopen-by-path matters only against a same-user local attacker who already owns the user's files; never observed. Rule 4d's own-box clause covers agent, hook, gate and drain machinery only. The finding stays open as it was before the triage.\n<!-- ledger-meta {\"command\":\"annotate\",\"effect_lines\":1,\"effect_sha256\":\"4c2175d5168731852eecb3f9b7ae392674c79c2bc8bdae9035ba41f55e8a9144\",\"input_sha256\":\"b2709c0e5979b7be13f55b09f5bc22158cf7c455b7ec6d5ae50ec378a8e49dc4\",\"kind\":\"mutation-receipt\",\"operation\":\"905ba259eb1d921ef219d921001600090ed09ab23717fb2f5d00308c33c276bd\",\"options\":{\"section\":null},\"request_id_sha256\":null,\"results\":[\"f-20260920-01\"],\"target\":\"f-20260920-01\",\"v\":1} -->\n\n## Threat model and non-goals\nOrdinary user or concurrent rename/replacement of parents or leaf objects after resolution or validation. Preserve no-follow containment, expected identity, existing repository exclusion, POSIX-lock safety, durability and bounded catalog provenance. No malicious continuous-unlink attacker, new public capability, schema migration, resource timer, framework or UI/product change. Ordinary database path validation must stay strict.\n\n## Traced premises\nCurrent source at18098b7b plus findings-only tier record. resolved.rs puzzle_database_target clones held parent and leaf then canonicalizes the old path. DatabaseFileTarget::probe_current reopens the pathname parent. Puzzle SQLite reads use private snapshots from held files. Puzzle cache_key constructs its blocking carrier before its blocking closure. Catalog publication verifies registered root and staging and inventories it, then resolved.atomic_install_download_dir drops both boundaries into pathname atomic_install_dir. Shared install_dir_at_driver and platform install_dir_at already accept held parent and expected source identity. Source trace is RUN/probe-windows-joiners.txt. Existing deletion fallback already covers straightforward rename, so the historical deletion claim is narrowed.\n\n## Approach\n### O1 — Keep a resolved puzzle's retained boundary\nA resolved puzzle read or delete mints its repository carrier from its already-held parent, leaf and file identity without reopening the pathname. That carrier probes the retained boundary without opening and closing the leaf, preserving pooled Unix POSIX locks. Replacing the leaf fails closed. Renaming or replacing the original parent spelling does not redirect the read. Path is a diagnostic/cache locator, never fresh authority. Ordinary database carriers retain existing strict pathname and parent revalidation. Express the internal distinction explicitly with a private validation policy chosen only by the sealed carrier producers. No general exemption from stored-authority canonical acquisition or rebinding rules.\nAll blocking carrier construction and probing for cache_key runs inside its existing cancellation-aware blocking closure. Snapshot reads, cache invalidation, exclusion and cancellation preserve existing contracts.\n\n### O2 — Install through the exact catalog-validated boundary\nFinal catalog publication carries the verified staging parent, staging leaf and exact inventoried identity into installation. The destination capability verifies that source and retained destination parent are the same object, and installs the validated leaf onto its own retained destination leaf through the shared descriptor-relative driver. A substituted pathname never becomes the install authority. Replaced source identity refuses. Existing provenance persistence, precommit failure, rollback and committed durability uncertainty retain their semantics.\nUse one narrow shared held-parent installation facade for both this path and existing OwnedStagingDir installation, retaining commit-aware cleanup. No new pathname-based helper, duplicate platform installer or weakening of current same-parent and no-follow checks.\n\n## Decisions and trade-offs\nOptimal: distinguish already-resolved puzzle capability validation explicitly and carry catalog-validated staging descriptors through final publication → I recommend this approach. Existing strict ordinary acquisition decisions d-20260918-18 and d-20261016-07 remain. d-20260912-04 still governs sites that require canonical_binding, but already-resolved puzzle targets do not acquire a second authority. d-20261005-05 governs inner extraction, which is not changed. New material policy is recorded through findings.py after plan approval with reversal path. Keep one original adopted f021 phase and its historical review metrics unchanged. This is a separate follow-up capability slice required by Ranking6, not a rewrite of O1–O4.\n\n## Risks / open questions\nThe main design judgment is the sealed distinction between ordinary strict-path and puzzle retained-parent probes. Review it before implementation. Native Windows runtime remains mandatory. Existing Windows held handles may refuse rename, so tests must assert the actual refusal rather than claim a Unix rename occurred. Added owned-source identity must remain tied to the inventory and parent that validated it.\n\n## Not part of this task\nNo ordinary database policy change, deletion redesign, SQLite connection framework, catalog ownership expansion, custom source verifier addition, tooling changes or renderer changes. Frozen f021 cleanup rules and legacy-directory preservation stay.\n\n## Phases\nOne cohesive capability phase, because producers and shared carrier/installer consumers share mod.rs/resolved.rs/infra/fs.rs/catalog_install.rs. Also puzzle.rs for blocking cache-key integration and direct runtime regressions. Sensitive Codex gpt-6.1-sol/high writer, one persistent context, no overlapping write leaves. Root traces/arbitrates/records/commits, separate Codex read-only lenses review, no family separation.\nPROOF: cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --locked infra::path_authority::tests -- --nocapture, cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --locked catalog_install -- --nocapture, cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --locked puzzle::tests -- --nocapture, cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --locked infra::fs::tests -- --nocapture, cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --locked db:: -- --nocapture, cargo fmt --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml -- --check, git diff --check. Behavioral tests cover puzzle carrier/cache/load after parent rename, substitute-parent isolation, replacement leaf refusal, and catalog substitution after inventory validation plus replaced staging. Unix source-only fix-revert red/green retains tests, no false Windows runtime claim. Existing ordinary parent-swap and pooled-lock tests stay green. Root pre-review, cumulative diff lenses, complete Rust final gates and exact-SHA Windows/macOS/platform CI precede installation. Original full three-flag gates already passed, new source is Rust-only and selected gates follow published corrective range.\n\n## Reviews\nRevision J1, no previous review, no open issue IDs yet. Read-only source probe is locate evidence, not approval. Plan authorship and arbitration share root context. Detection runs on same model family as code in separate sessions.\n",

  "native-source-commit-probe-analysis.md": "# Disposable native source commit measurement\n\nThis is a diagnostic artifact, not an approved mechanism or implementation. No production logic changed. The temporary test has been removed and infra/fs.rs restored byte-for-byte. Source at the measured HEAD bad4c6390898bc11043be5d641cfa3da57d3d201 matches source anchor 432dbc1e, as recorded by the empty source-anchor diff.\n\n## Actual native route and result\n\nThe probe used a real TempDir, OwnedStagingDir::adopt and install_staging_dir_at with DirectoryInstallPolicy::Absent. The source was adopted only at creation. A retained original directory descriptor measured the accepted identity and bytes. The existing AtomicDirInjector completed exactly one rename of the original source to a sibling, created a new directory at the original source leaf and wrote distinct unverified bytes at InstallRename. There was no fake filesystem, OS adapter, new hook or production branch.\n\nActual route in restored source:\n\n- infra/fs.rs:5570 install_staging_dir_at compares retained parent identities, drops the owner's child descriptor and calls unix::install_dir_at with its accepted source identity and a local committed flag.\n- infra/fs.rs:2292 unix::install_dir_at delegates to install_dir_at_driver.\n- infra/fs.rs:891 the driver performs its final source stat comparison. The final target comparison follows. Neither passes a source entry into commit.\n- infra/fs.rs:920 the driver calls the Unix adapter's commit with source_name and target_name.\n- infra/fs.rs:2256 InstallRename runs after those comparisons, immediately before renameat_with at line 2262. The absent-target arm uses NOREPLACE. This confines the target collision behavior, but does not bind the source name to an expected inode.\n- infra/fs.rs:932 the actual commit returning Ok sets committed=true. Parent sync follows and the result was Ok.\n- infra/fs.rs:5609-5610 the facade disarms the real owner only if its actual local committed flag is true. The probe observed disarming and reached the post-commit ParentSync hook. It did not directly expose the private local variable.\n\nObserved Linux values from the retained complete test output:\n\n| Object/state | Native observation |\n| --- | --- |\n| Held parent identity | (64513, 91619388) |\n| Accepted source and retained original pin | (64513, 91619389) |\n| Substitute created at source leaf | (64513, 91619403) |\n| Source leaf after syscall | Absent |\n| Installed target identity | (64513, 91619403) |\n| Moved original identity | (64513, 91619389) |\n| Installed bytes | UNVERIFIED-SUBSTITUTE |\n| Original pin and moved-original bytes | VERIFIED-ORIGINAL |\n| Installer result | Ok(()) |\n| Committed state | true, proven by the facade's actual disarmed state and post-commit phase |\n| Owner after call | armed=false, child=None |\n| Drop removal-attempt delta | 0 |\n| After owner drop | Wrong installed target and moved original both unchanged |\n\nAll descriptors were closed and the disposable root was removed before the correctness assertion. The completed test then failed with status 101 at NATIVE_SOURCE_COMMIT_UNVERIFIED_PUBLICATION. Compilation succeeded. No child engine or other external process was created by the fixture. The test's refusal branch was a diagnostic acceptable outcome, not approval of a future post-syscall disposition policy. The observed red depends only on Ok with the wrong installed identity.\n\n## Read-only mechanism seams after restoration\n\n### Windows accepted source entry\n\nWindowsDirEntry at infra/fs.rs:3615 retains its native File in _pin. directory_entry_at opens a directory at line 3634 with child_delete_access(true). That access is DIRECTORY_ACCESS | DELETE at line 2894, and DIRECTORY_ACCESS includes GENERIC_READ, GENERIC_WRITE, READ_CONTROL and SYNCHRONIZE at lines 2387-2393. The observed entry therefore already has the rename access required by rename_child.\n\nrename_child at line 2791 sends NtSetInformationFile(FileRenameInformationEx) to the supplied source handle. Its _temp_name parameter is not used for source lookup. Only the destination name and retained destination parent enter the rename buffer. A private commit contract carrying the accepted source Entry with the mutable access required by the current rename_child signature can therefore reuse that handle and avoid the current fresh source_name open at line 3801. If the accepted object has been moved to another sibling, renaming its handle may publish the original accepted object and leave the substitute at the old source leaf. Proof must permit that successful exact-original outcome. Windows runtime behavior was not measured here.\n\n### Unix post-syscall detector\n\nThe current Unix facade offers a parent-relative source-name rename, not a descriptor-source rename. The retained accepted source_dir and source_entry are available in install_dir_at_driver. The narrow existing seam for detecting a completed source substitution is after adapter.commit returns and physical committed=true has been recorded, before parent-sync reporting and before cleanup_displaced can delete an old target. Compare the installed target binding to the accepted source entry through the existing no-follow observation/identity operations. A mismatch must not reach trusted Ok, executable registration, or destructive displaced-tree cleanup.\n\nThis is detection after namespace mutation. It does not prove that an unverified directory was never transiently visible at the destination. It also does not solve malicious continuous mutation. The frozen unlink limitation is not evidence authorizing this rename residual.\n\nPhysical commit and trusted acceptance must remain separate facts. Returning a mismatch error from the adapter before the driver learns that the syscall committed would leave the facade's committed flag false and its cleanup armed, which would be a false precommit account. The actual rename must remain accounted for even if trusted publication is refused. A content/binding mismatch is not itself a parent-sync failure, so it must not be described as an otherwise valid install whose durability alone is uncertain.\n\n### Caller and retry consumers\n\ncatalog_install.rs:647 publishes provenance containing the accepted staging identity and inventory before final install. It rechecks source identity at line 720 and calls ResolvedPath::atomic_install_download_dir. That method at resolved.rs:237 uses the retained destination parent/leaf and absent-only installer. A final syscall substitution is downstream of those checks.\n\nfs.rs:1496 calls publish_engine_archive_tree on the same blocking worker that owns staging. An error reaches report_download_error at line 1519 and returns from the command. sanitize_download_error at line 826 only replaces raw Io diagnostics, leaving Conflict and CommittedDurabilityUncertain typed. error.rs categorizes Conflict as conflict and committed durability uncertainty as durability. src/platform/errors.ts maps those categories to validation and applied-despite-error respectively. The Tauri facade unwrapCommand throws command errors.\n\nsrc/utils/engines.ts:368 awaits downloadEngineArchive before registerInstalledEngineHandle and getEngineConfig. Thus a current mismatch error prevents that invocation from registering or probing an executable. The register helper's applied-error recovery is separate from the archive download call.\n\nHowever, fs.rs:1449-1452 checks only that an existing target is a real directory and returns successful adoption without re-extraction. archive_destination_directory_exists at infra/fs.rs:376 rejects symlinks and wrong-kind targets but does not verify inventory or content. A later install invocation can therefore accept a wrong directory left at the final destination by a mismatch error. register_installed_engine at mod.rs:6843 verifies a regular executable under the root, captures its actual identity and registers that object. It does not compare it with the signed archive digest or the old managed-tree inventory.\n\nThe prior provenance record is not a mismatch refusal fence. protect_catalog_contexts only refuses confirmed membership in a cleaning record at catalog_install.rs:602. collect_catalog_install forgets a record when the actual top-level target identity differs at lines 813-817, preserving the substitute. These are existing conservative cleanup semantics, not permission to promote the substitute as a verified catalog install.\n\n## Questions for root and fresh judgment\n\n1. Does the required Unix guarantee prohibit any transient raw final-name exposure, or require that only the validated object can receive trusted publication, registration and later adoption? A post-syscall identity detector can address the latter boundary for this measured completed substitution, but cannot claim the former.\n2. If Unix rejects after the rename, what accepted disposition preserves the moved original, substitute and any displaced old destination while preventing later existence-only adoption of the unverified final tree? Leaving it at the final name and merely returning Conflict is incomplete. A preserving no-replace move back or quarantine is an option requiring its own identity, failure, durability and retry proof. It is not an inode-conditional source rename and is not approved here.\n3. If that preserving recovery cannot complete, what existing or newly approved contract prevents later adoption and truthfully represents physical commit plus failed trusted acceptance? Existing cleaning ownership cannot silently be granted to an unverified substitute, and CommittedDurabilityUncertain must not assert content validation that failed.\n4. How must ordinary replacement preserve the displaced old target when post-syscall validation fails? The detector must run before existing destructive cleanup, and any rollback/recovery must preserve the same physical commit and parent-sync facts.\n\nNo option was implemented or selected by this leaf. Native Windows and macOS runtime proof remains outside this Linux measurement.\n\n## Inspected paths and evidence\n\nRead the named retained rules, windows-source-commit-mechanism.md, windows-source-commit-judgment.txt and lens-tauri-security-r11.txt. Source tracing inspected src-tauri/src/infra/fs.rs, src-tauri/src/infra/path_authority/resolved.rs, catalog_install.rs, mod.rs, src-tauri/src/fs.rs, src-tauri/src/error.rs, src/utils/engines.ts, src/platform/tauri.ts and src/platform/errors.ts. The foreign handoff was hashed for preservation only.\n\nThe addition and restoration patches are Git-derived. The reverse hunk's exact old coordinates and content were checked against the modified file, and reconstructed bytes were compared against the initial snapshot before apply_patch. No offset or fuzzy restoration was used. The complete initial and restored source SHA256 is 7dc67fb5584eec3d8106aefc895f4871ee52c1db7661f2a886c2954d1cf33bd1. Final cargo fmt --check and git diff --check both exited 0. Source diff is empty and the foreign handoff is unchanged. The disposable test is not left in the repository.\n",

## WSC3 final mechanism closure before implementation

All9 WSC3 plan lenses completed and APPROVED after full candidate/delta, measured probe, prior failed mechanisms and actual consumers. WSC-I1 explicitly CLOSED at plan level, WSC-I2 remains CLOSED, CR21 Windows handle mechanism CLOSED at plan level. No new adopted finding, Skip, Defer or open mechanism. Private judgment counts wsc1=2 wsc2=0 wsc3=0, not a replacement for original r1–r4, J1–J3 or R11=4. d-20261016-17 selects exact native confirmation plus durable pending/confirmed state in the existing registry, consumed by actual adoption and startup, preserving all foreign trees and existing child/session/cleanup evidence. One cohesive sensitive repair follows on the same persistent writer, no source edit yet. R11 CR18–21 all remain open code obligations until actual proof/closure, native Windows/macOS acceptance and release still pending.

Plan authorship and arbitration shared one context. Detection used same model family as code in separate Codex sessions, without family separation. Final approved snapshot and raw exact reports below make this independent of ignored plan and temporary artifacts.

{
  "source-publication-candidate-wsc3.md": "# Confirmed catalog publication and adoption\n\n## Goal and fixed mandate\nClose the measured final source substitution and subsequent retry-adoption gap in the active f-20261002-04 and co-located f-20260920-01 build. Preserve the original frozen O1–O4 and separate J3 retained-boundary mandate, with conservative ownership, interruption safety, D9 same-verified-artifact adoption and no deletion of user trees. No new product, threat, storage service, public command or runtime collector.\n\nAuthority for this substantive correction is original O1's verified native publication with durable provenance before rename, original O3's preservation of foreign trees and truthful retries, and J3 O2's exact inventoried source installation. Native Linux probe proves one completed source substitution yields Ok for an unverified tree. WSC2 and caller trace prove a post-check error alone allows ordinary retry to adopt it. The durable state below is necessary correctness under the already frozen interruption and filesystem-substitution threat, not an additional acceptance criterion used as authority.\n\n## O1 — Confirm the exact accepted source before trusted publication\nThe shared driver passes its accepted source observation into platform commit. Windows renames the already observed DELETE-capable entry handle, with no fresh source-name open. A completed source rename can validly publish that original object while preserving the substitute. Unix retains the existing name-based syscall, then the shared driver confirms installed identity against accepted source through existing no-follow observation before success, applied-durability reporting or displaced-tree cleanup.\n\nThe existing committed flag records physical rename immediately, independently of trusted acceptance. A wrong, missing or unconfirmable installed target returns ordinary path-free Conflict, never an applied-despite-error result. Preserve original, substitute and displaced target, with no destructive cleanup or unsafe pathname rollback after failed confirmation. Source-owner disarming follows actual mutation. Exact confirmed source keeps normal parent-sync/cleanup uncertainty semantics. No claim of zero transient namespace exposure on Unix or an inode-conditional rename primitive. Native application publication and adoption must remain fenced as O2 requires. Deliberate ongoing mutation beyond the frozen threat is not added.\n\nBoth platform adapters, standalone installer tests and OwnedStagingDir facade share this contract through the one existing driver. Group related installer inputs to remove its unsupported new too_many_arguments suppression, without a second driver or framework.\n\n## O2 — Keep unconfirmed publication fenced through retry and restart\nRepresent pending versus confirmed publication explicitly in each existing bounded catalog provenance record. Persist pending state with the accepted root, destination, source identity and complete managed inventory before any publication rename. Do not broaden ownership or deletion authority to a substitute. Only exact source publication and a durable confirmation transition may return normal installation success. A verified physical install whose confirmation persistence fails returns the existing applied-durability error truthfully, while durable pending evidence still protects retry. Native mismatch or unconfirmable installed identity remains a hard failure, and pending evidence cannot be erased merely because that rejected target differs from expected source.\n\nBefore the actual catalog command reports existing-target adoption, consult pending evidence under authority serialization for the exact authorized root binding and destination. A pending record permits adoption only after the expected tree identity and full original inventory have been re-proven and confirmation is durable. An existing mismatched, incomplete, modified or unconfirmable pending target refuses adoption, registration and probing with existing typed errors. This applies to an ordinary retry in the same process and after reopen, even if the earlier backend died before detecting the wrong syscall result. Share the confirmation predicate and transition between publication completion, retry adoption and startup handling, rather than maintaining parallel interpretations.\n\nStartup must preserve pending mismatch evidence and all foreign trees. It may retire an attempt after observing the destination absent through its exact held root. It may confirm an exact matching completed tree and then apply ordinary owner/session/cleanup rules. Lack of trusted owner absence still prevents collection. Pending state never authorizes deleting a substitute, and ordinary confirmed-tree replacement/modified/legacy preservation remains as before. Existing cleanup-in-progress refusal and retained original inventory cannot be canceled by adoption or a confirmation transition.\n\nBackwards compatibility: registries without catalog records load unchanged. Existing provenance records without a publication state require conservative interpretation, with no claim of confirmation from a folder name or mere existence. Re-prove exact root/tree/full inventory before automatic confirmation. Existing recorded cleanup-in-progress is evidence that the old collector already observed the original exact managed tree, remains adoption-blocked and preserves its original cleanup retry/completion semantics. An ambiguous older record must preserve its tree and evidence rather than silently promoting a foreign target. No migration program, format-version bump, second journal, timer, sweep or new retention quota. Existing record, admission, JSON-byte, inventory and session bounds remain ratchets.\n\nD9 still adopts prior confirmed same-artifact trees and unrecorded legacy directories without replacement or new ownership inference. Known pending/rejected publication is evidence that a directory has not earned successful-install status, so it cannot use that existence-only shortcut. This repairs a known failed attempt, and does not retrofit ownership into legacy folders. If an interfering target cannot be safely removed from the final name, leave it intact and retain the bounded pending fence. Normal startup and unrelated installs continue. No new manual process inspection or marker-clearing operation is required.\n\nExisting root-unavailable/replaced handling stays conservative and exact-binding based. Do not let an old pending record block a separately authorized independent root just because the path spelling is equal. Preserve the accepted root identity and all old session users through any same-destination retry, without transferring deletion ownership to another object.\n\n## O3 — Keep the admitted preparation boundary and one validator\nCR18: actual shared deadline helper tests must hold a real publication receiver while a pending admission future owns the sender. At timeout the admission future drops before awaiting the producer, and physical worker cleanup completes before assertions, including a deliberately reverted-source failure. An admitted publication tail can exceed preparation deadline and still return its real result. Preserve the broader actual download cancellation/deadline/native-operation test.\n\nCR19: one private prepared-tree validator owns hook, cancellation and staging-parent identity checks for both current consumers, preserving their order and standalone replacement semantics. CR20 groups coherent driver inputs. These are the other adopted R11 corrections in the same subsystem, not new policy.\n\n## Integration, costs and removal path\nFiles: src-tauri/src/fs.rs, src-tauri/src/infra/fs.rs, src-tauri/src/infra/path_authority/catalog_install.rs, and only the necessary private adoption/retained-boundary consumers in mod.rs/resolved.rs. Existing platform assertion tests only when an actual changed consumer needs faithful adaptation. No renderer, generated binding, manifest, workflow, tool, rule, quota or coverage/bundle baseline change.\n\nOne cohesive repair phase, because prepublication state, native commit confirmation, adoption and startup interpretation cannot ship disconnected. The same persistent sensitive Codex writer implements, no overlapping writers. Root arbitrates and owns independent proof, records, review, final gates and release. Additional state adds one durable confirmation transition after verified publication and preserves a bounded refusal when interrupted publication cannot be proven. Its observed benefit is preventing the measured wrong-tree success and retry adoption, its failure cost is a conservative error with all trees preserved. Reversal/removal requires another measured native publication/adoption protocol proving the same crash/retry and foreign-tree guarantees, then remove the superseded state/consumers together. No extra agent tool or gate is added.\n\nThe actual fs.rs download core must gate both early adoption and serialized publication before returning success. src/utils/engines.ts awaits that command before registration/config probing. Existing Conflict, committed-durability and diagnostic mappings stay, no new IPC error family. A mismatch cannot be reported as a valid install with durability alone uncertain. Confirmation persistence failures after a verified physical commit must not be disguised as precommit failures, and existing unresolved-durability handling must continue refusing unproven handoffs.\n\n## Verification and delivery\nUse actual native production paths and existing injectors. Linux final-window substitution must be an executed old-source behavioral red101, corrected hard failure with truthful committed/owner state, no applied result and no deletion. Continue through a normal retry and reopen using the actual archive core, proving no success, new substitute handle or engine probe, and that startup preserves the refusal fence. Cover a crash-equivalent pending record before post-check, exact valid pending recovery, durable confirmation-write failure/retry, absent pending completion, legacy state load and existing cleanup-in-progress semantics. Normal confirmed same-artifact and unrecorded legacy adoption stay successful and never replace or acquire ownership.\n\nWindows native final-window substitution must prove exact retained-source publication with substitute preservation, or genuine native5/32 refusal with original bytes intact. That routine returns Ok(false) after observing the target absent, with no confirmed transition. One completed target rename after the native driver's confirmation but before catalog confirmation can therefore return ordinary publication success without a confirmed target. This is source evidence in the unfinished phase, not an observed native failure or a committed regression. The approved WSC3 O1/O2 already requires missing or unconfirmable publication to fail hard. Root will require the same writer to consume false as a path-free Conflict and exercise the actual publication route at the existing postcommit ParentSync seam, preserving the moved original and pending evidence. No new architecture or acceptance scope is selected. The finding remains open pending implementation, review and native acceptance.\n"}

{"artifact": "publication-confirmation-consumer-test-only-delta.patch", "sha256": "bd9466e21d54a7524a4d291b94df47f7f3b716860b021a9fa91226580904e84d", "raw": "diff --git a/src-tauri/src/infra/path_authority/catalog_install.rs b/src-tauri/src/infra/path_authority/catalog_install.rs\nindex 73dd7aec..4ca71319 100644\n--- a/src-tauri/src/infra/path_authority/catalog_install.rs\n+++ b/src-tauri/src/infra/path_authority/catalog_install.rs\n@@ -1328,6 +1328,88 @@ mod tests {\n         assert!(f.adopt(\"managed\").unwrap());\n     }\n \n+    #[cfg(unix)]\n+    #[test]\n+    fn catalog_install_publication_confirmation_missing_after_commit_is_hard() {\n+        use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;\n+\n+        struct MoveInstalled {\n+            installed: PathBuf,\n+            moved: PathBuf,\n+            moves: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize>,\n+        }\n+        impl AtomicDirInjector for MoveInstalled {\n+            fn inject(&self, point: AtomicDirFaultPoint) -> std::io::Result<()> {\n+                if point == AtomicDirFaultPoint::ParentSync {\n+                    fs::rename(&self.installed, &self.moved)?;\n+                    self.moves.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);\n+                }\n+                Ok(())\n+            }\n+        }\n+\n+        let mut f = Fixture::new();\n+        let mut stage = f.stage();\n+        let accepted = stage.owner.binding().2;\n+        // Moving back to the former staging leaf makes disarming observable. An armed\n+        // owner would still recognize this exact original and delete it when dropped.\n+        let moved = stage.path().to_path_buf();\n+        let installed = f.root.join(\"managed\");\n+        let moves = Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0));\n+        set_test_atomic_dir_injector(Some(Box::new(MoveInstalled {\n+            installed: installed.clone(),\n+            moved: moved.clone(),\n+            moves: moves.clone(),\n+        })));\n+        let result = f.publish_stage(\"managed\", &mut stage);\n+        set_test_atomic_dir_injector(None);\n+        drop(stage);\n+\n+        let identity_after_owner_drop =\n+            fs::metadata(&moved).map(|metadata| (metadata.dev(), metadata.ino()));\n+        let engine_after_owner_drop = fs::read(moved.join(\"engine\"));\n+        let network_after_owner_drop = fs::read(moved.join(\"data/network\"));\n+        f.reopen();\n+        let pending_after_reopen = f.authority.catalog_installs.len() == 1\n+            && f.authority.catalog_installs.values().all(|record| {\n+                record.publication == Some(Publication::Pending)\n+                    && (record.identity.a, record.identity.b) == accepted\n+            });\n+        let untrusted = f.reconcile(vec![], false);\n+        let retained_without_trusted_absence = f.authority.catalog_installs.len() == 1;\n+        let trusted = f.reconcile(vec![], true);\n+        let retired_after_trusted_absence = f.authority.catalog_installs.is_empty();\n+        let final_engine = fs::read(moved.join(\"engine\"));\n+        let final_network = fs::read(moved.join(\"data/network\"));\n+        let final_identity = fs::metadata(&moved).map(|metadata| (metadata.dev(), metadata.ino()));\n+        let target_absent = !installed.exists();\n+        let move_count = moves.load(Ordering::SeqCst);\n+        let Fixture {\n+            temp, authority, ..\n+        } = f;\n+        drop(authority);\n+        temp.close().unwrap();\n+        eprintln!(\n+            \"MISSING_PUBLICATION_PROBE result={result:?} accepted={accepted:?} moves={move_count} identity_after_owner_drop={identity_after_owner_drop:?} final_identity={final_identity:?} pending_after_reopen={pending_after_reopen} retained_without_trusted_absence={retained_without_trusted_absence} retired_after_trusted_absence={retired_after_trusted_absence} target_absent={target_absent} all native cleanup completed before assertions\"\n+        );\n+\n+        assert!(matches!(result, Err(Error::Conflict(_))),\n+            \"MISSING_PUBLICATION_MUST_NOT_SUCCEED: absent publication must be a hard conflict, never success or applied uncertainty: {result:?}\");\n+        assert_eq!(move_count, 1);\n+        assert_eq!(identity_after_owner_drop.unwrap(), accepted);\n+        assert_eq!(engine_after_owner_drop.unwrap(), b\"managed engine\");\n+        assert_eq!(network_after_owner_drop.unwrap(), b\"managed network\");\n+        assert!(pending_after_reopen);\n+        untrusted.unwrap();\n+        assert!(retained_without_trusted_absence);\n+        trusted.unwrap();\n+        assert!(retired_after_trusted_absence);\n+        assert!(target_absent);\n+        assert_eq!(final_identity.unwrap(), accepted);\n+        assert_eq!(final_engine.unwrap(), b\"managed engine\");\n+        assert_eq!(final_network.unwrap(), b\"managed network\");\n+    }\n+\n     #[test]\n     fn catalog_install_publication_confirmation_absent_pending_attempt_retires() {\n         let mut f = Fixture::new();\n"}

{"artifact": "publication-confirmation-proof-native-identity.patch", "sha256": "84aca655b34e7a41ef6cf5c152e1afb24cdbf897977386673f870cc7f4f9490b", "raw": "diff --git a/src-tauri/src/infra/fs.rs b/src-tauri/src/infra/fs.rs\nindex 4c188f6f..85727735 100644\n--- a/src-tauri/src/infra/fs.rs\n+++ b/src-tauri/src/infra/fs.rs\n@@ -949,6 +949,13 @@ fn install_dir_at_driver<A: DirInstallAdapter>(\n             other => other,\n         })?;\n     *committed = true;\n+    if !matches!(entry_identity_at(parent, target_name, true),\n+        Ok(actual) if actual == adapter.entry_identity(&source_entry))\n+    {\n+        return Err(Error::Conflict(\n+            \"directory publication could not be confirmed\".into(),\n+        ));\n+    }\n     #[cfg(test)]\n     if let Err(error) = inject_atomic_dir(AtomicDirFaultPoint::ParentSync) {\n         log::warn!(\"directory installation parent sync failed: {error}\");\n"}

{"artifact": "publication-confirmation-proof-pending-adoption.patch", "sha256": "57bb90a4e418d020f4661a9b89e84addb29fb96b6ceb4b6886533f3329add5cb", "raw": "diff --git a/src-tauri/src/infra/path_authority/catalog_install.rs b/src-tauri/src/infra/path_authority/catalog_install.rs\nindex b6dd8367..e9cd12e7 100644\n--- a/src-tauri/src/infra/path_authority/catalog_install.rs\n+++ b/src-tauri/src/infra/path_authority/catalog_install.rs\n@@ -671,6 +671,7 @@ impl PathAuthority {\n         let path = resolved.target().ok_or_else(invalid_record)?;\n         let root = self.catalog_destination_root(destination, path)?;\n         self.protect_catalog_path(path, false, false, None)?;\n+        let confirmed = self.confirm_catalog_destination(&root, path)?;\n         let directory =\n             open_verified_directory(&root.path.to_path()?, (root.identity.a, root.identity.b))?\n                 .into_file();\n@@ -683,7 +684,7 @@ impl PathAuthority {\n         )?;\n         match entries.first() {\n             None => Ok(false),\n-            Some(entry) if entry.kind == DirectoryEntryKind::Directory => Ok(true),\n+            Some(entry) if entry.kind == DirectoryEntryKind::Directory && confirmed => Ok(true),\n             _ => Err(Error::Conflict(\n                 \"archive destination is not a directory\".into(),\n             )),\n"}

mut f = Fixture::new();\n+        f.install(\"managed\");\n+        f.reopen();\n+        let guard = scoped_test_removal_injector(Arc::new(Mount));\n+        assert!(f.reconcile(vec![], true).is_err());\n+        assert!(f.root.join(\"managed/engine\").exists());\n+        assert_eq!(f.authority.catalog_installs.len(), 1);\n+        drop(guard);\n+        f.reconcile(vec![], true).unwrap();\n+        assert!(!f.root.join(\"managed\").exists());\n+    }\n+\n+    #[test]\n+    fn catalog_install_depth_refusal_keeps_record_and_foreign_contents() {\n+        let mut f = Fixture::new();\n+        f.install(\"managed\");\n+        let mut deep = f.root.join(\"managed\");\n+        for _ in 0..MAX_REMOVE_TREE_DEPTH {\n+            deep = deep.join(\"deep\");\n+            fs::create_dir(&deep).unwrap();\n+        }\n+        fs::write(deep.join(\"foreign\"), b\"keep\").unwrap();\n+        f.reopen();\n+        assert!(matches!(\n+            f.reconcile(vec![], true),\n+            Err(Error::ResourceLimit(_))\n+        ));\n+        assert!(deep.join(\"foreign\").exists());\n+        assert_eq!(f.authority.catalog_installs.len(), 1);\n+    }\n+\n+    #[cfg(unix)]\n+    #[test]\n+    fn catalog_install_symlink_addition_preserves_foreign_target() {\n+        let mut f = Fixture::new();\n+        f.install(\"managed\");\n+        let foreign = f.temp.path().join(\"foreign\");\n+        fs::write(&foreign, b\"keep\").unwrap();\n+        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&foreign, f.root.join(\"managed/link\")).unwrap();\n+        f.reopen();\n+        f.reconcile(vec![], true).unwrap();\n+        assert_eq!(fs::read(foreign).unwrap(), b\"keep\");\n+        assert!(f.root.join(\"managed/engine\").exists());\n+        assert!(f.authority.catalog_installs.is_empty());\n+    }\n+\n+    #[cfg(target_os = \"linux\")]\n+    #[tokio::test]\n+    async fn catalog_install_running_uci_game_survives_upgrade_and_unconfirmed_restart() {\n+        use crate::engine::{EngineActor, EngineDeadlines, EngineSupervisor, GoMode};\n+        use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;\n+        let mut f = Fixture::new();\n+        let stage = f.stage();\n+        fs::write(stage.path().join(\"engine\"),\n+            b\"#!/bin/sh\\nwhile IFS= read -r line; do case \\\"$line\\\" in uci) echo uciok;; isready) if [ -f data/network ]; then echo readyok; else exit 3; fi;; go*) echo 'bestmove e2e4';; quit) exit 0;; esac; done\\n\").unwrap();\n+        fs::set_permissions(\n+            stage.path().join(\"engine\"),\n+            fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o700),\n+        )\n+        .unwrap();\n+        f.publish_stage(\"old\", stage.path()).unwrap();\n+        let old = f.engine(\"old\");\n+        let executable = f\n+            .authority\n+            .engine_executable(&old, PathOperation::EngineExecute)\n+            .unwrap();\n+        let actor = Arc::new(\n+            EngineActor::spawn_initialized(executable, EngineDeadlines::default())\n+                .await\n+                .unwrap(),\n+        );\n+        let supervisor = EngineSupervisor::default();\n+        let key = crate::game::game_side_engine_key(\"catalog-game\", 1, \"white\", \"owner\").unwrap();\n+        supervisor\n+            .replace_handle(\n+                key.clone(),\n+                actor.clone(),\n+                \"owner\".into(),\n+                old.path_ref().clone(),\n+            )\n+            .await\n+            .unwrap();\n+        f.install(\"new\");\n+        let new = f.engine(\"new\");\n+        supervisor\n+            .retire_engine_binary(\n+                \"owner\".into(),\n+                old.path_ref().clone(),\n+                new.path_ref().clone(),\n+            )\n+            .await\n+            .unwrap();\n+        f.reconcile(vec![new.path_ref().clone()], true).unwrap();\n+        f.reopen();\n+        f.reconcile(vec![new.path_ref().clone()], true).unwrap();\n+        assert!(f.root.join(\"old/data/network\").exists());\n+        actor.ensure_ready().await.unwrap();\n+        let request = actor.start_search(&GoMode::Depth(1)).await.unwrap();\n+        assert_eq!(\n+            actor.next_search_line(request).await.unwrap().as_deref(),\n+            Some(\"bestmove e2e4\")\n+        );\n+        assert!(supervisor.get_exact(&key).is_some());\n+        supervisor.terminate_all().await.unwrap();\n+        f.authority.clear_catalog_session_use().unwrap();\n+        f.reopen();\n+        f.reconcile(vec![new.path_ref().clone()], true).unwrap();\n+        assert!(\n+            f.root.join(\"old/data/network\").exists(),\n+            \"later sessions cannot erase unresolved origin use\"\n+        );\n+    }\n+}\n"}

fs::rename(f.root.join(\"managed\"), f.root.join(\"MANAGED\")).unwrap();\n+            f.reopen();\n+            assert!(\n+                f.adopt(\"managed\").unwrap(),\n+                \"native f.install(\"managed\");\n+            let inventory = f\n+                .authority\n+                .catalog_installs\n+                .values()\n+                .next()\n+              .into_file();\n+                let entries = read_directory_entries_at(\n+                    &directory,\n+                    &CancellationToken::new(),\n+                    None,\n+                    &mut |_| true,\n+                )\n+                .unwrap();\n+                // Block deletion in the last native top-level entry, allowing an earlier\n+                // entry to be physically removed before the real sharing refusal.\n+                let last = entries.last().unwrap();\n+                let blocked = if last.kind == DirectoryEntryKind::Directory {\n+ catalog_install_publication_confirmation_valid_pending_recovers_durably() {\n         let mut f = Fixture::new();\n"}

        ));\n+                assert_eq!(\n+                    fs::read(f.root.join(\"original/engine\")).unwrap(),\n+                    b\"managed engine\"\n+                );\n+            }\n+ fs::read(upper.join(\"witness\")).ok().as_deref()\n+            == Some(b\"independent native alias witness\".as_slice());\n+        fs::remove_dir_all(lower).unwrap();\n+        writeln!(\n+            std::io::stderr().lock(),\n+            \"R12_NATIVE_CASE_ALIAS applicable={applicable} root={:?}\",\n+            f.root\n+        )\n+        .unwrap();\n+        applicable\n+    }\n+\n+    #[test]\n+    fn catalog_install_r12_native_alias_adoption_and_pending_confirmation() {\n+        for state in [\"legacy\", \"confirmed\", \"pending\"] {\n+            let mut f = Fixture::new();\n+            if !r12_native_case_alias_applicable(&f) {\n+                return;\n+            }\n+            match state {\n+                \"legacy\" => {\n+                    fs::create_dir(f.root.join(\"managed\")).unwrap();\n+                    fs::write(f.root.join(\"managed/engine\"), b\"managed engine\").unwrap();\n+                }\n+                \"confirmed\" => f.install(\"managed\"),\n+                _ => f.pending_install(\"managed\"),\n+            }\n+            let record_count = f.authority.catalog_installs.len();\n+            fs::rename(f.root.join(\"managed\"), f.root.join(\"MANAGED\")).unwrap();\n+            f.reopen();\n+            assert!(\n+                f.adopt(\"managed\").unwrap(),\n+                \"native {state} alias must adopt\"\n+            );\n+            assert!(f.adopt(\"MANAGED\").unwrap());\n+            assert_eq!(f.authority.catalog_installs.len(), record_count);\n+            assert!(f\n+                .authority\n+                .catalog_installs\n+                .values()\n+                .all(|record| record.publication == Some(Publication::Confirmed)));\n+            f.reopen();\n+            let engine = f.engine(\"managed\");\n+            f.reconcile(vec![engine.path_ref().clone()], true).unwrap();\n+            assert_eq!(\n+                fs::read(f.root.join(\"MANAGED/engine\")).unwrap(),\n+                b\"managed engine\"\n+            );\n+            assert_eq!(f.authority.catalog_installs.len(), record_count);\n+        }\n+    }\n+\n+    #[test]\n+    fn catalog_install_r12_native_alias_pending_mismatch_survives_startup() {\n+        for alteration in [\"modified\", \"replacement\", \"file\"] {\n+            let mut f = Fixture::new();\n+            if !r12_native_case_alias_applicable(&f) {\n+                return;\n+            }\n+            f.pending_install(\"managed\");\n+            if alteration != fs::create_dir(f.root.join(\"managed\")).unwrap();\n+                }\n+            }\n+            let contents = if alteration == \"file\" {\n+                \"managed\"\n+            } else {\n+                \"managed/engine\"\n+            };\n+            fs::write(f.root.join(contents), b\"unconfirmed foreign contents\").unwrap();\n+            fs::rename(f.root.join(\"managed\"), assert_eq!(f.authority.catalog_installs.len(), 1);\n+                assert!(f\n+                    .authority\n+                    .catalog_installs\n+                    .values()\n+ format!(\"{name}/engine\")\n+                    };\n+                    assert!(matches!(\n+                        f.authority\n+                            .register_installed_engine(&f.handle, fs::read(f.root.join(if alteration == \"file\" {\n+                        \"MANAGED\"\n+                    } else {\n+                        \"MANAGED/engine\"\n+                    }))\n+ catalog_install_r12_native_alias_confirmed_cleanup_completes() {\n+        let mut f = Fixture::new();\n+        if !r12_native_case_alias_applicable(&f) {\n+            return;\n+        }\n+        f.install(\"managed\");\n+        fs::rename(f.root.join(\"managed\"), f.root.join(\"MANAGED\")).unwrap();\n+        f.reopen();\n+        f.reconcile(vec![], true).unwrap();\n+        assert!(f.authority.catalog_installs.is_empty());\n+        assert!(!f.root.join(\"MANAGED\").exists());\n+    }\n+\n+    #[test]\n+    fn catalog_install_r12_native_alias_partial_cleanup_and_preserved_refusal() {\n+        #[cfg(unix)]\n+        use crate::infra::fs::{scoped_test_removal_injector, RemovalFault, RemovalFaultPoint};\n+        for modified in [false, true] {\n+            let mut f = Fixture::new();\n+            if !r12_native_case_alias_applicable(&f) {\n+                return;\n+            }\n+            f.install(\"managed\");\n+            let inventory = f\n+                .authority\n+                .catalog_installs\n+                .values()\n+                .next()\n+                .unwrap()\n+                .inventory\n+                .clone();\n+            f.reopen();\n+            #[cfg(unix)]\n+            let fault = scoped_test_removal_injector(Arc::new(RemovalFault(\n+                RemovalFaultPoint::AfterEntryRemoved,\n+            )));\n+            #[cfg(windows)]\n+            let fault = {\n+                use std::os::windows::fs::OpenOptionsExt;\n+                use windows_sys::Win32::Storage::FileSystem::{FILE_SHARE_READ, FILE_SHARE_WRITE};\n+\n+                let record = f.authority.catalog_installs.values().next().unwrap();\n+                let directory = open_verified_directory(\n+                    &f.root.join(\"managed\"),\n+                    (record.identity.a, record.identity.b),\n+                )\n+                .unwrap()\n+                .into_file();\n+                let entries = read_directory_entries_at(\n+                    &directory,\n+                    &CancellationToken::new(),\n+                    None,\n+                    &mut |_| true,\n+                )\n+                .unwrap();\n+                // Block deletion in the last native top-level entry, allowing an earlier\n+                // entry to be physically removed before the real sharing refusal.\n+                let last = entries.last().unwrap();\n+                let blocked = if last.kind == DirectoryEntryKind::Directory {\n+                    f.root.join(\"managed\").join(&last.name).join(\"network\")\n+                } else {\n+                    f.root.join(\"managed\").join(&last.name)\n+                };\n+                fs::OpenOptions::new()\n+                    .read(true)\n+                    .share_mode(FILE_SHARE_READ | FILE_SHARE_WRITE)\n+                    .open(blocked)\n+                    .unwrap()\n+            };\n+            let cleanup = f.reconcile(vec![], true);\n+            drop(fault);\n+            #[cfg(windows)]\n+            assert!(\n+                matches!(&cleanup, Err(Error::Io(cause)) if matches!(cause.raw_os_error(), Some(5 | 32))),\n+                \"actual native delete-sharing refusal required: {cleanup:?}\"\n+            );\n+            assert!(cleanup.is_err());\n+            let record = f.authority.catalog_installs.values().next().unwrap();\n+            assert!(record.cleaning);\n+            assert_eq!(record.inventory, .unwrap()\n+            .into_file();\n+            let remaining = super::inventory(&directory, record.root.identity.a).unwrap();\n+            drop(directory);\n+            assert!(\n+ fs::rename(f.root.join(\"managed\"), f.root.join(\"MANAGED\")).unwrap();\n+            if modified {\n+                fs::write(f.root.join(\"MANAGED/user\"), b\"preserved user addition\").unwrap();\n+            }\n+            f.reopen();\n+            assert!(matches!(f.adopt(\"managed\"), Err(Error::Conflict(_))));\n+            f.reconcile(vec![], true).unwrap();\n+ .register_installed_engine(&f.handle, \"managed/user\"),\n+                        Err(Error::Conflict(_))\n+                    ));\n+                    assert_eq!(\n+
